**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Place replay evidence outside the checkout**

This workflow always passes an output directory inside `${{ github.workspace }}`, but `discovery-lab-reproduce.mjs` explicitly rejects any output path within the repository. With `set -o pipefail`, the command exits with `Choose an evidence directory outside this repository`, fails the job, and prevents the browser acceptance command on the next line from running.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve parents by a unique campaign identity**

When the same finite result is rerun, especially after only the installed source digest changes, its `resultDigest` remains identical because the bindings and attempt ID are not part of the result. Although `discoveryBridge.run` authorizes that some matching campaign has current source bindings, this `find` selects the earliest matching campaign, which can be an older source-bound record; the successor is then constructed and exported with the wrong parent ancestry. Bind `parentDigest` to a unique attempt or to a digest that includes the campaign bindings.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin the byte-hashed source closure to LF**

On a checkout where these newly included modules have CRLF line endings, `visit()` reads them as text and hashes the newline-normalized `source.encode()`, while `verify_packaged()` and `capture_capability_operator()` later hash the raw bytes. The new paths are not pinned with `text eol=lf` in `.gitattributes`; converting only `discovery-lab.mjs` to CRLF reproduces a manifest digest that differs from the source file, causing validation and release packaging to fail on such checkouts. Pin every closure member to LF or compute the catalogue digest from the same raw bytes the validators use.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve symlinks before enforcing output isolation**

Although the workflow now supplies `runner.temp`, the CLI's remaining boundary check is lexical: if an apparently external path such as `/tmp/evidence` is a symlink to a directory inside the repository, `relative()` begins with `..` and passes, but `mkdirSync()` and the later writes follow the symlink into the checkout. This defeats the explicit outside-repository guarantee and can contaminate or overwrite checkout evidence; resolve the existing output or its nearest existing parent to its real path before applying the boundary test.
